newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu said to favour Bezeq offering.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu said to favour Bezeq offering.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu favours selling shares in Bezeq Israel Telecom through an international public offering rather than to a strategic investor, Treasury sources said.
Netanyahu's position was voiced at a weekend meeting with ministers involved in the privatisation of the state-controlled phone monopoly.
The Communications Ministry favours a public offering while the Treasury prefers selling a stake in the company to a strategic investor, the sources said.
The final decision will be made by the interministerial privatisation committee, which has yet to convene since Netanyahu's government was formed in June.
Treasury sources said current plans call for an international public offering of about 25 percent of Bezeq, as had been decided by the previous Labour government.

The international offering had been postponed because the Communications Ministry and Cable & Wireless Plc have not been able to reach an agreement concerning future purchases of Bezeq shares by the British company.
C&W already holds 10 percent of Bezeq and the government fears that further purchases of shares by C&W could undermine the public offering.
